t: #3815 Design Auction System — Hash Maps with Lazy-Deleted Max Heaps
o: We must track, per item, the bids of many users, supporting insert/update/remove of a user's bid and querying the (amount, userId)-max bidder. The key subtlety: a user's bid is unique per item (replaced on re-add), and ties on amount go to the higher userId. Constraints (5*10^4 calls) mean each operation should be around O(log n). Example walkthrough: bids (1,7,5),(2,7,6) -> query returns 2; updating user 1 to 8 makes query return 1; removing user 2 leaves 1; item 3 has no bids -> -1.
k: Keep a global map (userId,itemId) -> amount as the source of truth for existence.
Per item, a max-heap keyed by (amount, userId) with lazy deletion answers queries in amortized O(log n).
An entry in the heap is stale iff its amount differs from the map (or the bid was removed).

a.n: Approach 1: Per-item hash map + linear scan
a.i: Store for each item a dictionary userId -> amount. A query scans all bids of that item for the maximum (amount, userId) pair. Simple and correct; worst case O(size of item) per query.
s: Maintain outer map itemId -> inner map userId -> amount.
add/update set the inner entry; remove deletes it.
Query iterates the inner map tracking best (amount, userId).
a.t: O(1) amortized updates, O(k) per query where k is the number of bids on the item.

a.n: Approach 2: Max-heap per item with lazy deletion
a.i: Push (-amount, -userId) into a per-item heap on every add/update. On query, pop entries whose amount no longer matches the authoritative map; the first matching top is the answer. Removed bids simply never match.
s: Map (userId,itemId) -> amount is the source of truth.
add/update: set the map and push (-amount,-userId) onto the item's heap.
remove: delete from the map only.
query: while heap top disagrees with the map, pop it; return top's userId or -1.
a.t: O(log n) amortized per operation — each heap entry is pushed once and popped at most once.

w: In an interview, start with the map-of-maps to establish correctness, then upgrade to the lazy-deletion heap for guaranteed logarithmic queries. Pitfalls: forgetting the tie-break by higher userId, treating update as adding a second bid, and forgetting that removed bids must stop matching in the heap. Follow-ups: support k-highest bidders (use an ordered set / balanced BST), or persist timestamps for bid history.
